Name: Param Parekh  
Course: BTech (2022-26) 
Branch: Electronics and Telecommunication engineering 
Reg. no: 221090049 
Company: Axxela Research and Analytics Private Limited 
Role: Trainee Analyst 
Location: Mumbai 
 
Eligibility:  
BTech - all branches 
CGPA >= 5 
X and XII >=50% 
No backlog 
 
Hiring Workflow: 
1.​ PPT 
2.​ Online Test 1 
3.​ Online Test 2 
4.​ Technical Interview 
 
Online Test 1: 
There were 4 sections and test was conducted offline on campus  
 
Section 1 - Behavioral questions 
Basic questions about trading in equities, risk-taking psychology, risk management 
techniques, personal questions like what would you do in this case 
 
Section 2 - Speed Maths 
​
Basic Algebraic problems 
​
6-8 algebraic problems combined into 1 question and such 5 questions 
​
Calculation is easy but very limited time is given so focus on speed and accuracy. 
​
Do mental math more over here to save time.

Section 3 - Numerical Aptitude 
Questions on number series, AP, GP, interest calculation, profit/loss calculation, 
direction-based questions, algebraic equation solving, ratio and proportion, train-crossing 
questions 
 
Section 4 - Logical Reasoning  
Age-based calculation, pattern-matching, mirror-image, find correct pattern sequence 
when cube is unfolded given 3 pictures of the cube, find blood relation based on other 
relations, Circular sitting arrangement on table and who is sitting next to whom, 
statement and conclusion type-of questions​ 
​
 
Online Test 2: 
After clearing Online Test 1, there was a virtual trading simulation round in CCF III. The main 
objective was to test profit-making skills based on a real-time demand-supply market scenario. 
Total 38 candidates including me qualified for this round. 4 groups of 8-10 candidates were 
formed by them (Axxela). Trading simulation was carried-out within the group. There were 9 
rounds; in each round a digit from a 9-digit number will be revealed. You have to quickly 
calculate the minimum and maximum possible number i.e. determine the range based on the 
already revealed digits and the remaining digits. Each digit from 0 to 9 will appear only once. 
Within the range you have to predict the most likely value based on the prediction in the previous 
round. First round will be spontaneous but slowly it will converge to some range of value. You 
have only 2 options “Buy” and “Sell”. On top right there will be a holdings section and total 
count section. Total count can only range from -2 to +2. Holdings section will show at what price 
you purchased. At any moment of time during the gameplay your aim should be to buy at the 
minimum possible price and sell at the maximum possible price so as to maximize the profit. All 
this while staying closer to the probable true price or else closer to the most common bidding 
range within the group. On your trading screen all the group member names and their buy/sell 
bid with price will be visible on which you have to keep a close eye as well as you have to keep 
in attention your holdings. A trade gets executed automatically whenever a buy and a sell order 
gets matched. My strategy was to neither buy more nor sell more so that I have both the options 
open all the time according to the situation i.e keep holdings count in range (-1 to +1). Buying 
adds one to the count and selling subtracts one from the count. However if the deal favours profit 
you can go to +2 or -2. I was not bidding for sell at very high price and waiting for it to be 
executed, which was done by most of the other candidates. I utilized something called as market 
momentum i.e. keep less margin but execute more number of trades, following the broader trend 
visible from available buy/sell bids. Because of this my total profit at the end of 9 rounds was 
significantly higher than others and I qualified for the Technical Interview round. In this round 
remember that the final score that will be displayed after 9 rounds will be different from the 
profit that you’ve made because more points are awarded for trading close to average bidding 
range and making profit rather than for bidding extraordinarily high or low. So you have to be 
vigilant all the times and tap quickly for the right trade. An instructional video is available on 
YouTube

Technical Interview: 
 
Technical interview was conducted at their Mumbai office at Lodha Supremus, Powai. I entered 
the interview room and the interviewer got angry because I was wearing sandals. This 
immediately made me nervous. I went in sandals because it was the monsoon month of August. 
He questioned whether it is the correct way to go for an interview. I got clueless here. However I 
said that during internship also I used to wear sandals because of monsoon and in fact everyone 
in the office used to wear sandals. There is a concept in corporate settings to carry formal shoes 
when travelling and wear those on reaching office. I was surprisingly unaware of this and 
therefore shocked. However the interviewer moved on and asked about my internship - what was 
my domain of work and what was my role and what was my stipend over there. I was into a data 
analytics firm where I had worked on structuring raw data using SQL and prepared business 
reports using Power BI. Later he asked why I did not get PPO there to which I replied stating that 
the minimum training period over there is 6 months for a full-time role and I worked for 2 
months according to our course format. Then he started asking about the stock market and 
whether have traded previously or not. I have long trading experience in the equity market. I had 
carried with me my trade logs (trading history) of the past two years. He checked and verified the 
prices in those. My most of the trades were profitable so I think this impressed the interviewer. 
He then asked about what technical indicators do I look at while trading. I explained all those 
namely MA, MACD, RSI, Bollinger bands, DMI, Stochastic oscillator along with how to 
interpret them for identifying market trends and making buy-sell decision. After this the 
interviewer asked a psychological question that what would you choose - a trading job or a tech 
job provided that within trading there will be a filtering and only 40% will survive after 1 year 
but after that earning prospects would be high and on other hand in tech there will be no filtering 
but earning prospects would also be limited. To this I answered that I would choose a trading job. 
I gave reasoning that I have passion for trading, I have a family background in trading and 
brokerage and I believe that tech jobs are prone to many external factors like geopolitical 
up-downs and AI developments which are a kind of threat while on the other hand in a trading 
job only my skills and performance in terms of profit/loss matters. So in this point of view a 
trading job is more secure than a tech job. However he did not look convinced and started to 
counter by saying that your resume strongly says that you are a tech enthusiast then how will you 
perform in the trading industry. I countered by saying that technological tools equip traders in 
making well-informed decisions so tech background will prove beneficial for a trading role. He 
countered by saying that it applies to investment banking certainly but this is a prop trading firm 
so it might not be suitable for you. To this I replied that this role as well as the company are very 
well suitable for me because I perform well in fast-paced and individualistic environments as 
demanded by this role. It is evident from my resume also. After that he said checking his laptop 
that my scores in the test were good and asked what my strategy was in the trading simulation. I 
explained my thinking as stated in the previous section and I believe it impressed him. Then he 
asked a mental math question “78*79=?” to which I calculated as 78*80 - 78 without pen/paper 
and answered 6162. Then he asked an analytical question “what is angle between hour hand and

minute hand at 3:15 pm ?”. To this I answered (without pen/paper) 7.5 degrees (according to 
ratio and proportion technique on 360 degree scale). After that he directly asked how much 
profits will you be able to make in this job to which I replied that over the past two years I have 
generated 7.7% of annualized return in retail equity trading without any professional training.  I 
also have diversified my portfolio across different asset classes for risk management. So with 
professional training sky is the limit. The interview lasted for 30-35 minutes. The interviewer 
was sharp and straight forward. The result was announced on the same day in the evening 
through mail and I was selected.  
 
Preparation strategy: 
 
●​ For Online Assessment practise Speed maths, mental maths, aptitude and logical 
reasoning questions of difficulty level “Hard” (like those in CAT Quant section) with 
strict time limit like 10 mins - 10 questions 
●​ For trading simulation round go through youtube video. 
●​ You must have real trading experience (with profits obviously) or at least good 
knowledge about the securities market.
